referred to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee
not printed Senate Tax, Business and Transportation Committee

NM-2026-SB283.aiSummary: The bill would expand New Mexico’s metropolitan redevelopment rules to include housing shortage areas. It would let local governments use these rules for more redevelopment projects and define housing shortage areas as places with too little affordable housing, high costs, low vacancy, or not enough multifamily or workforce housing. It would also exempt a qualifying multifamily property in a housing shortage area from property tax for up to 20 years.

NM-2026-SB233.title: HIGH-IMPACT TUTORING FOR SOME STUDENTS

actions.text: Sent to Senate Committees' Committee & Senate Education Committee & Senate Finance Committee

NM-2026-SB233.aiSummary: The bill would require New Mexico public schools to find 4th through 8th graders with math or reading scores in the bottom quartile and offer them high-impact tutoring. Schools would have to start tutoring within 30 days, use a trained tutor, keep groups to no more than four students per tutor, and provide it at least three times a week for at least 10 weeks. Parents would get notice, a written plan, progress reports, and guidance to help at home.

NM-2026-HB83.title: PERSONAL CARE SERVICES MEDICAID REIMBURSEMENT

actions.text: not printed House Rules and Order of Business Committee

NM-2026-HB83.aiSummary: The bill would require the state health care authority to set minimum Medicaid pay rates for personal care services. It would also require personal care services agencies to spend at least 70% of that Medicaid money on direct care worker costs like pay, benefits, and training, and keep records to show it. The bill includes a $51.4 million general fund appropriation for fiscal year 2027 to update the fee schedule and raise these payments.

NM-2026-HB301.title: JUDICIAL BRANCH INFO TECH PROJECTS

actions.text: not printed House Rules and Order of Business Committee

NM-2026-HB301.aiSummary: The bill would let the Department of Information Technology work on tech projects for courts and other parts of the judicial branch. It would also set up a yearly list of the tech goods and services the department can offer and the rates for them. The bill includes a $1.2 million state fund grant for the district attorneys' office to buy tech goods and services for district attorneys statewide.

NM-2026-HB289.title: SCHOOL TRANSPORTATION FUNDING

actions.text: Sent to House Education Committee & House Appropriations & Finance Committee

NM-2026-HB289.policyArea: EDUCATION, PUBLIC SCHOOLS, MOTOR VEHICLES (autos, trucks, buses, cycles)
NM-2026-HB289.aiSummary: The bill would change how New Mexico pays for school bus service for school districts and state-chartered charter schools. It would let transportation money cover the miles a bus travels to pick up the first student and to return after the last drop-off. It would also update how the state calculates each school’s transportation funding, with an effective date of July 1, 2026.

NM-2026-HB220.title: TIME OF SALE OR TRANSFER FOR DELINQUENT TAXES

actions.text: Sent to House Government, Elections and Indian Affairs Committee & House Taxation & Revenue Committee

NM-2026-HB220.aiSummary: The bill would give counties more time before turning over some delinquent property tax cases to the Taxation and Revenue Department, changing the period from more than two years to more than four years. It would also raise the wait time before real property can be sold for unpaid taxes from three years to five years. These changes would affect county treasurers, the department, and property owners with unpaid property taxes.
